readback.name: Poincare.ParabolicGraphTimeJets.finite_time_transfer
readback.mathematical_statement: For independent universes u,v, every R-normed vector space E:Type u, every finite type iota:Type v (possibly empty), arbitrary real alpha,T, G:Graph(E,alpha,T), a family W:iota->Graph(E,alpha,T), constant real coefficients a:iota->R, a fixed x:E, and fixed source points xs:iota->E, assume 0<T and the value identity G.u(s,x)=sum_i a(i)*W(i).u(s,xs(i)) for every s in [0,T]. Then for every t in [0,T], G.ut(t,x)=sum_i a(i)*W(i).ut(t,xs(i)). No alpha-range, completeness, finite-dimensionality, spatial compatibility, or coefficient/point time dependence is assumed. Graph supplies zero initial trace and genuine within-[0,T] time derivatives, so the result includes t=0 and t=T as well as interior times; T>0 excludes the degenerate singleton interval. The supplied premise is an all-time value identity at these fixed points, not a premise about time derivatives. The finite sum includes all iota entries and becomes zero when iota is empty. The statement gives time-jet transfer only; it does not assert spatial first/second derivative identities or a uniform bound. Each Y carrier uses the sup norm plus the supremum of scaled differences over distinct ordered pairs of points in [0,T]xE, with scale (||x-y||+sqrt(|s-t|))^alpha and zero inserted in the supremum sets. Each Graph has the sum norm ||u||_Y+||ut||_Y+||du||_Y+||ddu||_Y, using operator norms for the continuous-linear-map values; all four carriers are exactly zero outside [0,T]xE. These are the original norms, although the conclusion states no estimate.

readback.name: Poincare.ParabolicGraphTimeJets.tensor_time_covariance
readback.mathematical_statement: For arbitrary real alpha,T, any two nine-entry graph families U,V:Inputs(alpha,T)=(Fin 3 x Fin 3)->Graph(E,alpha,T) on E=EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), any spatial function phi:E->E, any fixed R-continuous linear map J:E->E, any z:E and real t, assume 0<T, t in [0,T], and that eventually for s in the within-interval neighborhood filter nhdsWithin t [0,T], tensorValue U(s,z)=pullbackBilinearForm(tensorValue V(s,phi(z)),J). Here tensorValue W(p)=sum over all ordered a,b in Fin 3 of W(a,b).u(p) times the continuous bilinear basis tensor E_ab, with E_ab(v,w)=v_a*w_b, so all nine entries are retained with no symmetry or off-diagonal convention. The pullback acts by H(v,w)->H(J(v),J(w)). Define TT W(p)=sum over all ordered a,b of W(a,b).ut(p) times that same E_ab. Then TT U(t,z)=pullbackBilinearForm(TT V(t,phi(z)),J), as an equality of actual continuous bilinear forms, equivalently in every pair of vector slots. Graph time derivatives are within [0,T], so the conclusion includes both endpoints. There is no alpha-range, regularity, injectivity, chart-source, or invertibility hypothesis on phi or J, and J is not asserted to be Dphi(z). Both phi(z) and J are held fixed when time is differentiated; no moving-map terms occur. The premise assumes local-in-time value covariance at the single fixed spatial pair z,phi(z); the theorem transfers it to time-jet covariance, and does not establish the value covariance itself or spatial-jet covariance. It asserts no norm estimate. This conditional transfer does not assume its derivative conclusion; trivial inputs such as J=0 give meaningful zero pullbacks and do not make the universally quantified statement vacuous. Each Y carrier uses the sup norm plus the supremum of scaled differences over distinct ordered pairs of points in [0,T]xE, with scale (||x-y||+sqrt(|s-t|))^alpha and zero inserted in the supremum sets. Each Graph has the sum norm ||u||_Y+||ut||_Y+||du||_Y+||ddu||_Y, using operator norms for the continuous-linear-map values; all four carriers are exactly zero outside [0,T]xE. These are the original norms, although the conclusion states no estimate. Inputs carries the original finite Pi maximum of its nine Graph norms.
